title: Polish Dative Case: Endings, Pronouns and Uses
excerpt: The Polish dative case (celownik) marks who receives something. Learn the endings, mi vs mnie, zimno mi, dative verbs and prepositions.
metaDescription: The Polish dative case (celownik) explained: komu? czemu?, endings for nouns and adjectives, mi vs mnie, zimno mi, podoba mi się, prepositions and exercises.
summary: The Polish dative case (celownik) answers komu? and czemu? and marks the person who receives, benefits from or feels something.
Singular endings are -owi (or -u for brat, ojciec, pan, kot, pies, Bóg, chłopiec) for masculine nouns, -e or -i/-y for feminine and -u for neuter; the plural is always -om.
Short pronouns mi, ci, mu are the default; use mnie, tobie, jemu at the start of a sentence, for emphasis and after prepositions (with niemu, niej, nim).
Impersonal phrases such as zimno mi, przykro mi, podoba mi się and nie chce mi się all put the person who feels it in the dative.
